actions: Continue the pilot of peak-hour mobile pickup slot limits with 20% of capacity reserved for in-café orders in the 50 pilot cafés through February 2027, maintaining current beverage pricing and not exceeding the two-hour staff addition per store per weekday.

Begin real-time release of unused reserved café-order capacity to mobile orders if not claimed within the first 5 minutes of each 15-minute window, but only in half (25) of the pilot cafés as an A/B test to compare guest experience and transaction completion rates.
expected_responses: Dutch Bros and Dunkin may intensify digital and value messaging, but are unlikely to materially change their offers until more evidence emerges from the Starbucks pilot.

Some mobile customers may experience improved slot availability and reduced abandonment in the A/B test stores, while café guests should see little to no negative impact if the release is managed tightly.
If the real-time release proves successful, competitors may attempt to mimic dynamic capacity allocation in their own digital channels.
content.rationale: Sustaining the current pilot maintains consistency for measurement and avoids prematurely expanding or rolling back before evidence is collected. Introducing a controlled A/B test of releasing unused reserved capacity allows Starbucks to probe whether tighter management of reservations can reduce mobile order abandonment and improve all-channel throughput without undermining the café experience. This balances the need to restore in-store credibility with digital convenience and tests a reversible, measurable operational tweak within binding constraints.
resource_commitments: Continue allocating up to two additional peak staff-hours per weekday per pilot café (max $60/store/day) for the duration of February.

Allocate digital and operations resources to implement and monitor the real-time capacity release in 25 pilot cafés, ensuring robust instrumentation of order attempts, slot fills, capacity release, and customer completion rates.
